summary: This document defines PKCS #8 content types for PrivateKeyInfo and EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo, as specified in RFC 5958. This gives such key files standard identifiers.

eli5.summary: Private keys can be stored in files, and this gives official names for the kinds of key files so software can recognize them.

questions: what is the oid for privatekeyinfo
subtitle: Gives private-key files two official identifiers so they can travel inside CMS messages.

tldr.problem: A PrivateKeyInfo or EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo could not be carried in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) without content type identifiers, and none had been assigned.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two object identifiers, id-ct-privateKeyInfo (52) and id-ct-encrPrivateKeyInfo (53), plus a small ASN.1 module that binds each to its structure.
tldr.outcome: IANA has assigned the identifiers, so one private key, plain or encrypted, can be carried as CMS content. The RFC adds no new security rules of its own.

today: RFC 9939 is a Proposed Standard, and no RFC obsoletes or updates it. It builds directly on RFC 5958, whose security considerations still apply.

sections.title: Why Key Content Types Are Needed
sections.content:
The syntax for private-key information was first described in RFC 5208 and later revised by RFC 5958. That revision added the AsymmetricKeyPackage content type, which supports several PrivateKeyInfo values at once.

This document covers the simpler case: one PrivateKeyInfo or one EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo. To be carried in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS, RFC 5652), each needs a content type assignment, and this RFC supplies them.

The RFC also notes that, a very long time ago, media types for the same two structures were assigned as application/pkcs8 and application/pkcs8-encrypted.
sections.eli5: A mail sorter needs a label on every parcel. Key parcels had no label yet, so this RFC makes two.

sections.title: The Two Content Types
sections.content:
Section 2 defines one content type for private-key information and one for encrypted private-key information. Each is named by an object identifier (OID), a dotted number path that is assigned once and means the same thing everywhere.

  • id-ct-privateKeyInfo identifies the PrivateKeyInfo content type. It sits under the S/MIME content type arc with final number 52.
  • id-ct-encrPrivateKeyInfo identifies the EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo content type, with final number 53.

Both live under the same parent path: iso, member-body, us, rsadsi, pkcs, pkcs-9, smime(16), ct(1).
sections.eli5: Each label is a long number, like a library call number. One number means a plain key and the next means a locked key.

sections.title: The ASN.1 Module
sections.content:
Section 3 gives the formal definition in ASN.1. The module builds on the modules in RFC 5911 and imports CONTENT-TYPE from the CMS module and PrivateKeyInfo and EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo from the module in RFC 5958.

It declares a set called PrivateKeyInfoContentTypes that holds ct-privateKeyInfo and ct-encrPrivateKeyInfo, followed by an extension marker (...) noting that more content types are expected. Each content type pairs a structure with its OID using IDENTIFIED BY.
sections.eli5: This part is the exact wording of the labels, written in a strict language so computers all read it the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The entire section is one sentence: the security considerations in RFC 5958 apply here. This RFC defines identifiers and adds no new mechanism, so it adds no new security text.
sections.eli5: The label does not change how safe the key is. The safety rules for the box are written in an older document.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA has assigned OID 52 to id-ct-privateKeyInfo and 53 to id-ct-encrPrivateKeyInfo in the registry for S/MIME CMS content types (1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.1). It also assigned 85 to id-mod-pkcs8ContentType, the identifier of the ASN.1 module, in the S/MIME module identifier registry (1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.0).

IANA also updated the application/cms media type entry. RFC 9939 is added to its interoperability considerations and to the list of RFCs that define inner content types, and privateKeyInfo and encrPrivateKeyInfo are added to the list of inner content types.
sections.eli5: IANA is the keeper of the official list. It wrote the new labels into the list so nobody else uses the same numbers.

items.label: id-mod-pkcs8ContentType
items.desc: Identifier of the ASN.1 module itself.
